courses.label: BIOL 31
courses.title: Biology for Engineers
paras: An introduction to the study of biology by the case history method with emphasis on the effects of environmental manipulation. 2 lectures, 1 hour laboratory, one term.

courses.label: BIOL 131
courses.title: An Introduction to Biology
paras: Life, the nature of protoplasm, cells and cellular processes. The structure and functioning of the flowering plant. The variety of plants, plant phylogeny. The role of macroflora and microflora in organic cycles. Animal characteristics, a survey of the animal kingdom. Human physiology. An introduction to genetics and evolutionary theory.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: BIOL 231
courses.title: Genetics and Evolution
paras: The principles, methods, and application of genetics. The implications of genetics in the modern evolutionary theory. 2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: BIOL 431
courses.title: Ecology
paras: An analysis of the freshwater, marine and terrestrial environments and the communities of organisms they support. The distribution and numbers of plants and animals, Animal movements and migrations.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: BIOL 601
courses.title: Water Pollution Biology
paras: A lecture, seminar, and practical course providing an introduction to the biological, chemical and engineering aspects of water pollution.

courses.label: BIOL 602
courses.title: Fisheries Biology
paras: A lecture and seminar course dealing with the basic techniques of fisheries biology and reviewing the significant literature in the field.

courses.label: BIOL 603
courses.title: Paleobotany
paras: A course dealing with the evolution of the plant kingdom, with emphasis upon the Fern-Pteridosperm complex and microfossils in the Pleistocene. Aspects of Phylogeny and paleobotany are studied.

courses.label: BIOL 604
courses.title: Advanced Physiology
paras: A seminar and reading course covering certain aspects of physiology and metabolism, growth and differentiation, with particular emphasis on selected topics in the field of the student’s research.

courses.label: BOTANY 231
courses.title: Plant Anatomy and Morphology
paras: The anatomy, morphology and taxonomy of the plant kingdom, with the life histories of typical examples. 2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: BOTANY 331
courses.title: Plant Physiology
paras: Study of respiration, photosynthesis, water relationships, nutrition, growth factors, etc., as fundamental physiological processes of the plant. 2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: BOTANY 431
courses.title: Microbiology
paras: A survey of microorganisms with special reference to the morphology, physiology and taxonomy of bacteria; also the microbiology of special environments.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: ZOOLOGY 231
courses.title: Vertebrate Zoology
paras: The evolution of the vertebrate body as exemplified by both living and fossil members of the group. Laboratory dissections form an integral part of the course.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: ZOOLOGY 332
courses.title: Vertebrate Physiology
paras: An integrated study of the concepts of the cell and its environment and the basic processes of living cells. The physiology of major organ systems of the vertebrate body with emphasis on the human.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: ZOOLOGY 431
courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology
paras: A survey of the major invertebrate Phyla with emphasis on the anatomy, taxonomy, and ecology of selected representatives. 2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHE 11
courses.title: Chemical Process Principles I
paras: Practice in applied stoichiometry. Mass and energy balances. The simple unit operations such as evaporation, drying, etc. Prerequisite: Chem 11.
3 lectures, 2 hours laboratory, problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 12
courses.title: Chemical Process Principles II
paras: Introduction to the unit operation concept. The mass and energy balance, utilizing physical-chemical principles, will be applied to the elementary unit operations of solution, dilution, evaporation, etc. Preliminary studies of the stage concept will be presented. Dimensional analysis and modeling are incorporated.
Prerequisite: ChE 11.
2 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 13
courses.title: Unit Operation Analysis
paras: Analysis and functional design of processing units for distillation, absorption, extraction, drying, humidification, leaching and crystallization.
Prerequisites: ChE 12, ChE 21.
2 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 21
courses.title: Transport Processes I
paras: The transport concept is introduced as a general theory. Fluid dynamics and heat transfer are presented from a co-ordinated basis of transport phenomena and thermodynamics.
Prerequisite: ChE 11. 3 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 22
courses.title: Transport Processes II
paras: Theory of diffusion, Navier-Stokes equations, interphase mass transport, phase transformation, simultaneous heat and mass transport and the analogy between them.
Prerequisite: ChE 21.
2 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 23
courses.title: Transport Processes III
paras: Momentum, energy, and mass transport phenomena and their inter-relationships.
Prerequisite: ChE 22.
3 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 31
courses.title: Physical-Chemical Principles
paras: Properties of solids, liquids, and gases. Introduction to thermodynamics and chemical kinetics with simple applications, The phase rule.
Prerequisite: Chem. 11.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CHE 32
courses.title: Thermodynamics I
paras: Principles of thermodynamics, Criteria of physical and chemical equilibria. Pressure-volume-temperature relations of fluids. Energy conversion.
Prerequisites: ChE 11, ChE 31.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 33
courses.title: Thermodynamics II
paras: Flow processes. Properties of real solutions. Vapor-liquid equilibria. Equilibria in chemical reactions.
Prerequisite: ChE 32.
3 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 34
courses.title: Thermodynamics III
paras: Physical and chemical equilibria of multicomponent systems. Introduction to statistical thermodynamics.
Prerequisite: ChE 33.
3 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 41
courses.title: Reaction Kinetics I
paras: Introduction to kinetics and mechanism of elementary chemical processes in homogeneous systems; reversible, consecutive and simultaneous reactions, interpretation of kinetic data, homogeneous catalysis, chain reactions. Prerequisites: ChE 12, ChE 31.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 42
courses.title: Reaction Kinetics II
paras: Design of homogeneous batch and flow reactors; material balance in flow systems, differential and integral tubular reactors, graphical and algebraic methods for stirred reactor batteries.
Prerequisite: ChE 41.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 43
courses.title: Reaction Kinetics III
paras: Non-isothermal batch and flow reactors, semi-flow processes, heterogeneous reactions, scale up principles for reactors involving heat and mass transfer. n
Prerequisite: ChE 42.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 51
courses.title: Process System Theory I
paras: A co-ordinated approach to linear systems analysis is presented in an engineering format. The physical phenomena of the several fields are presented as analogs to establish a useful basis for system analysis in the process industries..
Prerequisites: Math 41, ChE 22.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 52
courses.title: Process System Theory II
paras: The material of Process System Theory I is extended to more complex processes. Closed loop systems are examined for stability. Advanced concepts in control systems are introduced. .
Prerequisite: ChE 51.
2 lectures, 3 problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 53
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control
paras: An examination of advanced control methods and their impact on process dynamics. ; fos ; : Prerequisite: ChE 52. ‘
3 lectures, pne term.

courses.label: CHE 61
courses.title: Industrial Economics, Market surveys, estimation of capital
paras: and operating costs of a new product or process. Economic feasibility studies and projected economic evaluation for processes in the various stages of research, development, and design. Appraisal of capital expenditures.
Prerequisite: ChE 12.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHE 62
courses.title: Process System Design
paras: The undergraduate curriculum is co-ordinated and brought together to accomplish the basic objective of the process engineer, the design of an integrated chemical process.
Prerequisites: All Chemical Engineering required courses.
2 lectures, 3 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CHE 71
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory I
paras: Experiments in the application of physical and chemical principles to engineering analysis, phase equilibrium, fluid flow and heat transfer.
Prerequisites: ChE 12, ChE 21.
4 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CHE 72
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory II
paras: Experimenta! studies with pilot plant equipment in the representative unit operations: evaporation, distillation, absorption, extraction, drying, humidification and reactors.
Prerequisites: ChE 13, ChE 71.
6 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CHE 73
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory III
paras: Chemical reactors, process dynamics steady-state and transient behaviour, and applications of digital and analog computors. Prerequisites: ChE 72, ChE 41, ChE 51.
6 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CHE 91
courses.title: Seminar
paras: Study and presentation of material in recent literature. 1 hour, one term.

courses.label: CHE 98
courses.title: Research and Design Project I
paras: 3 hours, one term.

courses.label: CHE 99
courses.title: Research and Design Project II
paras: Prerequisite: ChE 98. 9 hours, one term.

courses.label: CHE 601
courses.title: Applied Chemical Kinetics and Reactor Design
paras: A study of the kinetics of homogeneous and heterogeneous, catalytic and non-catalytic reactions. Primary emphasis is placed upon predicting the course of chemical reactions under the conditions of process operations and the application of the principles of reactions kinetics, heat, and mass transfer to the design of chemical reactors.
one term.

courses.label: CHE 602
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: A treatment from the engineering viewpoint of the volumetric and phase behaviour of pure substances and multicomponent systems at physical and chemical equilibrium. Estimation of thermodynamic properties from a knowledge of molecular structure. Emphasis will be on the application of these principles to the solution of problems in industria! practice.
one term.

courses.label: CHE 611
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Heat Transfer
paras: Analysis of unsteady state heat transfer in complex systems. Examination of high velocity and/or high temperature systems. Coupled mass and heat transfer as in boiling, transpiration and ablation.
one term.

courses.label: CHE 621
courses.title: Process Optimization
paras: The definition of the optimization problem in design and control. Introduction to applications of steepest ascent, calculus of variations and mathematical programming.
one term.

courses.label: CHE 622
courses.title: Process Dynamics
paras: Dynamic characterization of the process complex by experimental and simulation techniques. Non-linear, distributed parameter, positive feedback effects. Dynamics as a tool in advanced process theory and alanysis.
one term.

courses.label: CHEM 5
courses.title: Introductory Chemistry
paras: Fundamental theories, laws, and principles of general chemistry. Study of some non-metallic and metallic elements and their compounds illustrating the theory.
2 lectures, 4 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 11
courses.title: General Chemistry
paras: An elementary study of the states of matter, changes of state, solution laws. Atomic structure and chemical bonding; Stoichiometry of equations. Oxidation-reduction. Chemical equilibria. Descriptive inorganic chemistry.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 21
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry
paras: Systematic inorganic chemistry based on the periodic classification, with emphasis on the relationship between properties and structure. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 22
courses.title: Analytical Chemistry
paras: Principles of quanitative analysis; precipitation, titration, separation, complex formation. Experiments in classical and modern methods of analysis, and problems on the necessary calculations.
1 lecture, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 25
courses.title: Polymer Chemistry and Physics
paras: The organic and physical chemistry of elementary polymerization reactions. A study of the physical properties of polymeric materials as related to molecular structure. An introduction to polymer technology. Prerequisite: Chem 11 and Phys 15.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 26
courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
paras: The basic chemistry of the important classes of aliphatic and aromatic compounds. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 31
courses.title: Atomic and Molecular Structure
paras: Introduction to the quantum-mechanical theory of chemical bonding. Atomic and molecular orbitals. The spatial arrangements of atoms and molecules. Methods of structure determination. Covalent bond lengths and angles. Crystal chemistry of ionic substances. The stereochemistry of various elements and their compounds.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 35
courses.title: Electrochemistry
paras: Electrolytic conductance and transport. Thermodynamics of electrolytic solutions. Electrode potentials. The measurement of pH. Metallic corrosion. Prerequisite: ChE 32, Chemistry 22.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 36
courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
paras: An introduction to the important classes of heterocyclic compounds and natural products. A laboratory course on preparative organic chemistry and organic techniques accompanies the lectures.
Prerequisite: Chemistry 26.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 37
courses.title: Biochemistry
paras: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, hormones, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Metabolism of these groups of compounds. Physics-chemical aspects of biochemistry.
Prerequisite: Chemistry 36.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 41
courses.title: Nuclear Chemistry
paras: Structure, properties and reactions of nuclei. Quantitative treatment of radioactive processes. Radiation detection and measurement. Chemical applications.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 45
courses.title: Surface Phenomena
paras: A study of absorption, wetting, foams, electrical surface phenomena, and principles of heterogeneous catalysis.
Prerequisite.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 46
courses.title: Organic Chemistry III
paras: Selected topics on the chemistry of organic compounds of industrial interest.
Prerequisite: Chemistry 36.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 55
courses.title: Polymer Physics and Chemistry
paras: The chemistry and physics of natural and synthetic polymers, covering the following topics: condensation and addition polymers and their reaction kinetics; properties of polymers, their measurement and relation to structure; isotactic polymers, copolymers, and polymer reactions.
Prerequisite.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CHEM 131
courses.title: General Chemistry
paras: Elementary study of the states of matter, changes of state, solution laws; atomic structure and bonding; stoichiometry of equations, oxidation-reduction, chemical equilibria; descriptive chemistry of the commoner elements in terms of the periodic table.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 222
courses.title: Qualitative Analysis
paras: The principles of chemical separations and analysis: solubility product, ionization of weak acids and bases, hydrolysis or ions, formation of complex ions, oxidation-reduction. Reactions of the more common ionic species inaqueous solutions. The practical work consists of separation and detection of common cations and anions. Prequisite: General Chemistry.
2 \ectures, 3 hours laboratory. (Summer session only).

courses.label: CHEM 231
courses.title: Chemical Bonding and Structure
paras: Electronic structure of atoms; the periodic table; nature and classification of chemical bonding; bond energies and electronegativity scales; structure and shape of molecules; crystal structure of common inorganic substances.
2 lectures (For General students, 1 hour problem).

courses.label: CHEM 232
courses.title: Analytical Chemistry
paras: Theory and practice of elementary quantitative inorganic analysis; experiments to illustrate gravimetric, titrimetric, and absorptiometric methods; introduction to various methods of separation.
2 lectures, 6 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 235
courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
paras: An introduction to chemical thermodynamics including the laws of thermodynamics applied to simple systems of fixed composition. Approximately ten hours of the course will be devoted to an introduction to the phase tule. 2 lectures, 1 hour problems.

courses.label: CHEM 236
courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
paras: The properties, preparations, reactions, and basic structural theory of the common classes of aliphatic and aromatic compounds. A laboratory course on preparative organic chemistry accompanies the lectures.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 325
courses.title: Physical Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the study of matter from the macroscopic and molecular point of view. Classical kinetic theory of gases, thermodynamics, electrochemistry, kinetics, molecular structure, surface phenomena, phase equilibria and macromolecules.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 331
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry I
paras: Systematic inorganic chemistry stressing general forms of behaviour and periodic trends among the elements. Descriptive chemistry will be presented in part through reading assignments. The accompanying laboratory will illustrate methods of synthesis; analytical tests of products; and determination of composition, structure, and physical constants.
2 lectures, (For General students, 3 hours laboratory).

courses.label: CHEM 335
courses.title: Physical Chemistry I]
paras: The rate laws of elementary kinetics, complex reactions and catalysis. Electrochemistry and the thermodynamics of non-electrolytes. 2 lectures, 6 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 336
courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
paras: Chemistry 236 expanded to stress enolate condensations and alicyclic compounds, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms. The laboratory course includes further preparative work and qualitative organic analysis.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 337
courses.title: Biochemistry I
paras: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, hormones, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Metabolism of these groups of compounds. Physico-chemical aspects of biochemistry.
2 lectures. (For General students, 3 hours laboratory).

courses.label: CHEM 431
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry II
paras: Selected topics in inorganic chemistry including co-ordination chemistry, mechanisms of inorganic reations, nuclear and radiochemistry, non-aqueous solvent systems, high-temperature chemistry. The laboratory course includes preparation of typical inorganic compounds and physical measurements to establish structure and stability of these.
2 lectures, 6 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 435
courses.title: Physical Chemistry III
paras: The thermodynamics and kinetics of surface phenomena. An introduction to the fundamentals of quantum and statistical mechanics with applications to rate theories and small molecules.
2 lectures, 1 hour laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 436
courses.title: Organic Chemistry III
paras: A selection of more advanced topics to include heterocyclic compounds, natural products, and theoretical aspects of organic chemistry. 2 lectures.

courses.label: CHEM 437
courses.title: Biochemistry II
paras: Selected topics and techniques in modern biochemistry; energy transfer, transport across membranes, comparative aspects of metabolism, mechanism and kinetics of enzyme activity, structural macromolecules.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 439
courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
paras: Physical chemistry; or organic chemistry; or inorganic chemistry, for students in Honours Chemistry and Physics (cf. course 431). Three hours may be in Biochemistry (cf. course 437).
Chem. students, 6 hours laboratory.
Chem. & Phys. students, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: CHEM 445
courses.title: Polymer Chemistry
paras: The chemistry and physics of natural and synthetic polymers, covering the following topics: condensation and addition polymers and their reaction kinetics; properties of polymers, their measurements and relation to structure; isotactic polymers, copolymers, and polymer reactions..
2 lectures.

courses.label: CHEM 631
courses.title: Co-Ordination Chemistry
paras: Equilibrium and kinetic aspects of complex species experimental and calculative techniques; mechanism of reactions of co-ordination compounds.

courses.label: CHEM 632
courses.title: Chemical Analysis
paras: An advanced treatment of classical analysis. The application of equilibria and kinetic considerations to the study of deviations from stoichiometric behaviour. The formation and nature of precipitates, non-aqueous solvent methods, analytical separations.

courses.label: CHEM 635
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: A rigorous treatment of chemical thermodynamics with emphasis on the complete thermodynamic description of a system.

courses.label: CHEM 636
courses.title: Natural Products
paras: Selected topics in the field of natural products stressing the use of spectral and other physico-chemical methods in the determination of structure.

courses.label: CHEM 641
courses.title: Crystal Chemistry and Optical Goniometry
paras: The chemical significance of the structure of solids. Measurement of crystals to determine external symmetry and drawing of the conventional projections.

courses.label: CHEM 642
courses.title: Chemical Instrumentation
paras: Instrument components and optimum application; rudiments of design; electrical, spectral, migrational and other methods.

courses.label: CHEM 645
courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
paras: The fundamentals of quantum chemistry with applications to the solution of the wave equation for simple molecules and the solution by approximate methods for large molecules.

courses.label: CHEM 646
courses.title: Theoretical Organic Chemistry
paras: The structure and reactivity of organic molecules emphasizing stereochemistry and reaction mechanisms.

courses.label: CHEM 651
courses.title: X-Ray Crystallography
paras: Powder and single crystal methods of x-ray diffraction. The reciprocal lattice. Organic and inorganic examples. The use of radiation detector equipment. The approach to structural problems.

courses.label: CHEM 655
courses.title: Chemical Kinetics
paras: Statistical methods applied to the kinetic molecular theory and to the treatment of interacting systems. The kinetics of homogenous reactions in gases with emphasis on unimolecular reactions, and of reactions in condensed phases.

courses.label: CHEM 656
courses.title: Synthetic Methods of Organic Chemistry
paras: A discussion of classical and newer concepts in the synthesis of organic compounds with emphasis placed on the fundamental behaviour patterns. An integration of experimental facts and modern theories is presented.

courses.label: CHEM 665
courses.title: Chemical Spectroscopy
paras: Introduction to ultraviolet, infrared, and resonance spectroscopy, with emphasis on applications to studies of organic molecules.

courses.label: CIVE 11
courses.title: Engineering Graphics I
paras: The course is designed to teach manipulation of drawing instruments and to develop manual drafting skills. Problems include orthographic, axonometric, oblique, isometric, and perspective methods of graphic presentation.
4 hours, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 12
courses.title: Engineering Graphics II
paras: This course supplements the course in Engineering Graphics I with furrher instruction in graphical methods. Graphical methods for solving problems involving vector quantities. The design, construction, and use of graphs and special charts, with various applications. The use of specially graduated scales, and the design of slide rules and nomograms. Graphical and mechanical methods of integration. Prerequisite: CE 11.
4 hours, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 21
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids I
paras: Review of statics. An analytical treatment of the resistance of materials, commencing with definitions of strains, stress, and properties of idealized materials. Mohr’s circle for stresses. Elastic and plastic behaviour of members subjected to axial, shearing, torsional and flexural deformations. Columns, statically indeterminate systems, and combined stresses are also treated.
3 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 22
courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids II
paras: A general treatment of the behaviour of structural components from the study of stress and strain in solids. Topics include Mohr’s circle for strains and moments of inertia. Superposition, Castigliano’s theorem, theories of failure, elastic and inelastic analysis of unsymmetrica! bending, torsion, and columns. Curved beams, beam on elastic foundation, shear centre and torsion of cellular members. Various topics in theory of plasticity, limit analysis and elastic stability. Applications of numerical analysis.
Prerequisite: CE 22.
2 lectures, one term.
31. : Theory of Structures I. Analysis of simple determinate structures. Static and moving loads on beams and trusses. Conditions for statical determinacy. Deformation of trusses. Influence lines.
Prerequisite: CE 21.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 32
courses.title: Theory of Structures II
paras: Elastic and plastic analysis of indeterminate plane structures. Analysis of space structures. Methods of virtual work, slope deflection, moment distribution, and matrix analysis.
Prerequisite: CE 31.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 33
courses.title: Behaviour and Design of Metallic Structures
paras: Introduction to design, risk and the uncertainty in loads and material strength properties. The problem of rational design, Development of codes and specifications. Principles of elastic and limit design. Behaviour, analysis and design of structural elements in metal. Beams, tension and compression members, connections and plates. Design of simple structures. Experimental studies of structures.
Prerequisites: CE 22, 32.
3 lectures, 3 hours problems or laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 34
courses.title: Behaviour of Plain and Reinforced Concrete
paras: Physical and chemical properties of cements, water, and admixtures; design of concrete mixes, workability, strength, and durability; field procedures and control; laboratory work on test procedures and concrete technology. Behaviour, analysis and design of structural elements; beams, tension and compression members, design of simple structures; experimental studies of structures.
Prerequisites: CE 31, 51.
3 lectures, 3 hours problems or laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 35
courses.title: Structural Design
paras: Loads, safety, and rational design criteria relating to structural design, structural form and structural action. Economic proportions. Behaviour of integral structures and consideration of failure in real and ideal structures. Application to design.
Prerequisites: CE 33, 34.
2 lectures, 1 seminar, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 41
courses.title: Surveying
paras: Plane surveying with tape, transit, level, and compass. Field practice and applications. Corrections and adjustments. Computation of azimuths, errors, areas. and earth-work. Mapping. Horizontal and vertical curves, topographic surveying and mapping. Land surveying field astronomy, precise traverse and levelling.
3 lectures, 6 hours field work, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 42
courses.title: Surveying and Photogrammetry
paras: Advanced topics in surveying and photogrammetry. Aerial triangulation. theory of stereoplotters, stereotopographic mapping, application of photogrammetry other than from aerial photographs.
Prerequisite: CE 41.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 51
courses.title: Geology for Engineers
paras: An introductory course in geology, with emphasis on topics particularly related to civil engineering; mineralogy (particularly clay mincralogy), petrology, aggregates, structural geology, geomorphology (especially glacial geology), and ground water. Laboratory work will include the identification of minerals and rocks and the study of the use of geological maps for engineering purposes. Weather permitting, field trips may be undertaken in addition to the laboratory sessions.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 52
courses.title: Soil Mechanics
paras: Identification and classification of soils, index properties, capillarity and permeability, frost action, compaction, compressibility and consolidation, stress distribution, shear strength, pore pressure perameters, character of natural soil deposits, subsurface exploration and sampling, case histories. The lecture course is supplemented by a series of laboratory experiments on the techniques and interpretation of soil tests.
Prerequisite: CE 51.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 53
courses.title: Foundations and Earth Structures
paras: Soil investigation and surveys, shear strength-time relationships, flow nets, slope stability, earth dams, earth pressure theories, earth retaining structures, bearing capacity theories, bearing capacity and settlement with relation to shallow and deep foundations.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 61
courses.title: Highway Engineering I
paras: The planning, economics, finance, location, and design of transportation facilities. Highway and airport pavements, loads and stress distribution, soil strength, soil stabilization, drainage, behaviour and design of flexible and rigid pavements. The lecture course is supplemented by laboratory experiments on highway materials.
Prerequisite: CE 52.
3 lectures, 3 laboratory, alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 62
courses.title: Highway Engineering II
paras: Principles of highway location. Geometric design of highways and intersections. Traffic, maintenance and operations.
Prerequisite: CE 61.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 71
courses.title: Water Resources Engineering
paras: General introduction to the physical, chemical and biological bases of water treatment and waste water treatment and disposal. Principles of design and construction of facilities for the collection, treatment, and distribution of water, and the collection, treatment, and disposal of waste waters. The lecture course is supplemented by a series of laboratory experiments related to water quality measurement and process control.
3 lectures, 3¢hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 72
courses.title: Environmental Health Engineering
paras: An introductory course to the engineering principles which form the basis of environmental sanitation. Environmental health problems of the community and of industry are considered, including water, food, and air supplies, disposal of human and industrial wastes, animal and arthropod vectors, lighting, ventilation, noise, accidents, industrial poisons, and ionizing radiations. Prerequisite: CE 71.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 81
courses.title: Law, Contracts and Specifications
paras: Engineering law. The design and composition of contracts and specifications. 2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 82
courses.title: Urban Planning
paras: Urban and regional planning. The contro! and administration of land use for various purposes. Problems of regional planning and urban growth related to communications, etc.
Prerequisite: CE 61.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 83
courses.title: Project Management
paras: Separation of planning and scheduling functions, traditional methods, arrow diagramming, calculation of earliest and latest event times, design, delivery, and capital restraints, critical path determination, scheduling and calendar dating, the data flow cycle, linear progiamming and operational analyses. 3 lectures, one term.

84, Civil Engineering Design Studies I. Design of civil engineering projects, building structures, bridges, highway and municipal engineering works. Emphasis is given to the interrelationship between design synthesis, and the various sciences and disciplines covered in the undergraduate course of studies.
6 hours, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 85
courses.title: Civil Engineering Design Studies H. Advanced studies in civil engineering design synthesis, related to optional courses offered, and direction of special interest. 9 hours, one term

courses.label: CIVE 86
courses.title: Research Project
paras: Introduction to research problems and procedures, in various areas of civil engineering, with particular relation to special interests in optional programmes of students concerned.
9 hours, one term.

courses.label: CIVE 609
courses.title: Theory of Structures III
paras: Iterative methods in structural analysis. Advanced problems in stability of frames, trusses, and their components. Dynamic loadings and shock effects. Vibrations.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 610
courses.title: Inelastic Behaviour of Ductile Members and Structures
paras: Simple plastic theory and limit design of plane frames, plates, and space structures. Deflections. Shakedown. Inelastic instability and the influence of strain hardening. Dynamic loading.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 611
courses.title: Theory of Elasticity and Plasticity
paras: Complex variables and three-dimensional problems in spherical and cylindrical co-ordinates. Thermal stresses. Dynamics of elastic continua. Large deflection problems, Fundamental theorems of plasticity and limit analysis. Slip-line fields.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 612
courses.title: Experimental Mechanics
paras: Classification and estimation of errors. Smoothing of experimental data. Similitude and model laws. Simulation of frames, trusses, plates, and shells. Analogue methods in experimental stress analysis. Electrical and mechanical strain gauges, transducers. Brittle coatings. Photoelasticity.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 613
courses.title: Mathematical Methods in Applied Mechanics
paras: Calculus of finite differences. Applications to moments and deflections of beams. Problems of elastic stability. Beams on elastic foundation. Energy methods. Rayleigh-Ritz and Galerkin procedures. Solution of systems of linear algebraic equations by relaxation and the Crout method. Applications to statically indeterminate systems. Bending of plates.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 614
courses.title: Mechanics of Media
paras: A unified introduction to the mechanics of solids and fluids. Stress, deformation and flow. Materials and their rheological properties. The equations of elastic solids. Problems in linear elasticity. Equations of fluid mechanics. Problems in viscous and ideal fluid flow. Introduction to the analysis of shells. Problems in plasticity and theoretical soil mechanics. Application to geophysics.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 615
courses.title: Theory of Plates and Shells
paras: Differential geometry of surfaces. Equations of equilibrium and deformation in orthogonal curvilinear co-ordinates, Momentless theory of shells. Energy formulations and stability problems in shells. Limit analysis of plates and shells.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 640
courses.title: Highway Engineering (Planning and Design)
paras: Highway Planning—method and results; classification, needs, sufficiency ratings; economics of location; highway finance; highway administration; geometric design of roads and streets—principles and methods.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 641
courses.title: Traffic Engineering
paras: Basic characteristics of traffic, drivers, vehicles, volumes, speeds, delays, etc.; traffic studies; capacity determinations; traffic theory including interrelationships of land use and traffic; mathematical models.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 642
courses.title: Transportation Engineering (Urban Planning)
paras: Basic urban transportation studies including origin/destination, inventory, use, parking and transit studies; land use planning, travel desires; economics in urban transportation.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 651
courses.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
paras: Theories of elasticity and plasticity applied to soils. Advanced studies of research techniques in soil mechanics and foundation engineering. one term.

courses.label: CIVE 652
courses.title: Measurement of Soil Properties
paras: Laboratory and field work in soil sampling and testing. Measurement of soil mechanics parameters for design and research problems. Experiments include permeability, consolidation, direct shear, and triaxial shear.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 653
courses.title: Soil Engineering
paras: A critical study by the consideration of case histories of the current procedures for design and construction of foundations, earth retaining structures and earth slopes.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 654
courses.title: Engineering Aspects of Surficial Soils
paras: Use of geologic and pedologic information and airphoto interpretation principles and techniques in the prediction of eningeering properties of soils and the planning of engineering soil surveys.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 671
courses.title: Water Resources Engineering I
paras: Water Supply and Treatment. The unit operations involved in the treatment of water for domestic and industrial uses.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 672
courses.title: Water Resources Engineering II
paras: Waste-Water Treatment and Disposal. The physical, chemical, and biological processes utilized in the treatment of domestic and industrial waste-waters.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 673
courses.title: Water Resources Engineering III
paras: Advanced Laboratory-Water Quality Measurement and Process Control. A series of laboratory experiments on the various unit processes of water and waSte-water treatment. Stream pollution Investigations. one term.

courses.label: CIVE 674
courses.title: Water Resources Engineering IV
paras: Design and Operation of Water and Waste- Water Treatment Facilities. Practical design of the unit processes of water and wastewater treatment facilities. Design of a complete treatment facility. Operating problems in water and waste-water treatment plants and their elimination or minimization through proper design.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 675
courses.title: Air Resources Engineering
paras: The principles of the field of air pollution; health, nuisance, agricultural, etc., aspects; causes and sources; characteristic emission rates, gas flow in ducts and chimneys; physical properties of particulate matter; engineering design of air cleaning equipment; public relations, control ordinances, and zoning; public administration.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 681
courses.title: Environmental Sanitation
paras: Engineering problems in refuse collection and disposal, sanitation to suburbs, foods and milk sanitation, housing, industrial hygiene, and other environmental sanitation programmes.
one term.

courses.label: CIVE 698
courses.title: Special Directed Studies
paras: one term.

All the following courses are Honours courses, but any of them may be taken by students in General Arts, with the exception of Economics 450, 460 and 470.

courses.label: ECON 100
courses.title: Introduction to Economics
paras: A general survey course in the Principles of Economics. Among the topics discussed are the determination of prices, the measurement and determination of the level of national income and employment, the monetary and banking system, public finance and fiscal policy, labour unions, international trade, and Canadian economic problems.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 250
courses.title: Intermediate Economic Theory
paras: The theory of the firm, distribution theory, and the analysis of national income and employment. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 260
courses.title: Economic History of North America
paras: A study of the significance of economic factors in the growth of western civilization on the North American Continent with special reference to Canadian problems of staple production as shown in the fishing industry, the fur trade, lumbering, railroads and new techniques, wheat, mining, pulp and paper, and hydro electric power.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 350
courses.title: Money and Banking and National Income
paras: A study of the American, British and Canadian banking systems with particular reference to Canadian, central banking and monetary policies since 1935. Some time is also devoted to a discussion of the measurement and determination of the level of national income, employment and prices, money flow accounts, monetary and business cycle theory, the theory of inflation and international monetary economics.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 351
courses.title: Statistical Methods
paras: Collection, processing and analysis of quantitative data, tabular and graphical presentation and analysis of statistical data, frequency distributions, probability, sampling, linear regression and correlation, construction and use of index numbers; time series analysis.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 355
courses.title: International Economics
paras: The following topics are discussed in the First Term: Balance of Payments Statistics; The Economic Basis of Trade and Investment; Foreign Exchange Rates and their Determination; Commercial Policy; International Investment and Foreign Aid.
The Second half of the course studies the theory of international trade and investment, with special reference to the problems of economic development. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 360
courses.title: Labour Economics and Industrial Relations
paras: The history of trade unionism, collective bargaining, and the economics of the labour market. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 365
courses.title: Public Finance and Fiscal Policy
paras: The place of public expenditures and revenue in the national economy, taxation, debt management, and the role of fiscal policy in economic stabilization.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 370
courses.title: Industrial Organization and Public Policy
paras: Problems of monopoly and economic concentration with special reference to Canada. Government intervention in agriculture, public utilities, transport, and foreign enterprise. Public ownership and state planning.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 375
courses.title: National Income Analysis
paras: National Income Accounting; the Analysis of National Income; and, Problems of Economic Growth and Stability. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 450
courses.title: Advanced Economic Theory
paras: Analysis of the theories of representative economists.. Most attention is given to the writings of Marshall, Chamberlain and Keynes.
3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 455
courses.title: History of Economic Thought
paras: A survey of the historical development of economic theory. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 460
courses.title: Mathematical Economics
paras: Mathematical formulation of economic theory; an introduction to dynamic models and their solution; the use of linear systems in economic analysis; and, introduction to input-output analysis and linear programming. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECON 470
courses.title: Canadian Economic Problems
paras: A seminar devoted to the discussion of current Canadian economic problems and policies. 3 lectures.

courses.label: ECE 23
courses.title: Analogue Computation
paras: Basic analogue computing elements, computer diagrams and programming, scaling. Solution of linear and non-linear ordinary differential equations. Design aspects of computing components and operational amplifiers. Prerequisite: Math 31, Math 45.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 24
courses.title: Logic and Switching I
paras: The logcial design of relay and electronic switching circuits. Boolean algebra. Algebraic equivalent of switching logic; tables of combinations. Relay contact networks, elementary diode, vacuum tube, transistor, and magnetic core switching circuits.
Prerequisite: EE42, EE 52.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 25
courses.title: Logic and Switching II
paras: A course in engineering principles of stored programme digital computers. Design of arithmetic sections, coding, control. Over-all logical organization and memory techniques.
Prerequisite: EE 24.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 31
courses.title: Electromechanical Systems
paras: The analysis of electromechanical, hydraulic, and thermal systems through the terminal characteristics and inter-connections o! their components. Linear Graph and Matrix methods are used extensively. Prerequisite: Math 22.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ECE 32
courses.title: Electronics
paras: Principles and characteristics of vacuum and gas tubes, semiconductors, magnetic devices, and transducers; applications in industrial measurements and control.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ECE 41
courses.title: Network Theory I
paras: An introduction to the steady-state analysis of linear circuits—basic concepts of circuit parameters, series and parallel circuits and resonance, loop and nodal methods, network theorems.
Prerequisite: Math 22.
4 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 42
courses.title: Network Theory II
paras: Further study in steady-state extended to general analysis of circuits—balanced and unbalanced polyphase circuits, magnetically coupled circuits, complex waveforms, general forcing functions and transients.
Prerequisite: EE 41..
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 43
courses.title: Circuit Theory HII. A continuation of the general analysis of linear circuits ~—complex frequency and network functions, one-terminal-pair reactive networks, two-terminal-_pair reactive networks
paras: Prerequisite: EE 42.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 44
courses.title: Pulse and Switching Circuits
paras: The analysis of circuits used in the generation and shaping of non-sinusoidal waveforms—linear and nou-linear wave shaping and
gating, voltage and current sweep generators, multivibrators and the blocking oscilator.
Prerequisite: EE 43, EE 53.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 45
courses.title: Network Synthesis
paras: Energy Functions. Network functions; synthesis of assive one ports; introduction to the synthesis of LC and RC two ports. rerequisite: EE 43, Math 44 or Math 45.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 51
courses.title: Electronics I
paras: Electronic conduction and diodes. Semiconductor, vacuum and gas diodes. Resistive diode circuits. Piecewise-linear diode models. Simple multi-diode circuits. Rectification and detection. Capacitive and inductive ripple filters. Introduction to the transistor. os
Prerequisite: Math 22.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 52
courses.title: Electronics II
paras: Transistor models and circuits. Transistor voltage gain and current gain. Comparison of basic transistor circuits. Variation of transistor parameters. Introduction to the vacuum triode. Triode characteristic curves. Groundedcathode, cathode-follower and grounded-grid amplifiers. Tetrode and pentode control valves. Gas triodes.
Prerequisite: EE 51.
4 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 53
courses.title: Electronics IH. Comparison of vacuum triode and transistor amplifiers
paras: Analysis of RC-coupled amplifiers. Sine-wave, square-wave and ramp excitation of R' coupled amplifiers, Broad-band low-pass power amplifiers. Tuned amplifiers. Sinewave oscillators. Relaxation oscillators. A.M..and F.M. modulation and detection. Frequency conversion. Noise and signal-to-noise ratio.
Prerequisite: EE 52... -.
2 lectures, one term.

54, Microwave Circuit Theory. Electron motion in microwave tubes, Interaction between electron beams and alternating electric fields. Diodes and _grid-controlled tubes. Travelling wave tubes, Network representation of tubes. Tube noise, Prerequisite: EE 53, EE 72. .
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 55
courses.title: Solid State Electronics
paras: Crystal structure and imperfections; classical and quantum statistics, electron energy and distributions; Mobility and lifetime of electrons and holes; Current flows in semiconductor and in p-n juntions; Surface properties; Tunnel diode and parametric amplifiers.
Prerequisites: EE 43, 53.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 56
courses.title: Static Fields
paras: Electrostatics, boundary value problems, dielectric material, magnetostatics, vector potentials, The calculation of capacitance and inductance for typical structures.
one term.

courses.label: ECE 61
courses.title: Electromechanics I
paras: Magnetic circuits. Study of the commutating machine both in isolation and as a component in a d.c. control system. Terminal characteristics of the three modes of operation—generator, motor, and rotating amplifier; transient and steady-state analysis, Matrix methods are used extensively. 3 lectures, one term..

courses.label: ECE 62
courses.title: Electromechanics II
paras: Two-winding and multi-winding transformers. Equivalent circuits are derived from transformation theory. Study of a.c. machines from their terminal characteristics. Symmetrical component sequence equations are derived from a linear transformation. Matrix methods are used extensively.
Prerequisite: EE 61.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 63
courses.title: Electromechanics III
paras: Further study of a.c. machines. Derivation of forward and backward sequence components to enable steady state and transient analysis of synchronous and induction machines. Performance characteristics are derived analytically and experimentally.
Prerequisite: EE 62.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 64
courses.title: Advanced Electromechanics
paras: Advanced topics in rotating machinery. Direct and quadrature component analysis of a.c. machines. Extensive treatment of nonlinear characteristics of synchronous machines in steady-state; equations suited for transient analysis on the digital computer are derived.
Prerequisite: EE 63..
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 65
courses.title: Power Systems Analysis
paras: Systematic mathematical formulation of systems of polyphase machines, 3-phase transformers, and transmission lines in terms of the sequence variables. Analytical and computer solutions.
Prerequisite: EE 63.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 71
courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields I
paras: Electrostatic and magnetostatic laws in differential and integral forms, and boundary conditions, Electrostatic problems in different co-ordinate systems. Maxwell equations. Energy relationships. Circuit concepts and Mzxwell’s equations. Propagation of plane waves. Guided waves in coaxial cables, arallel-plates and waveguides of simple structures. rerequisite: Math 41, Phys 13.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 72
courses.title: Electromagnetic Fields II
paras: Transmission lines, network concepts of waveguide and cavities. Integration of Maxwell equations, and far-zone or near-zone approximations. Fields produced by antennas of simple current sources, Antenna arrays. Impedance concepts of antenna, Aperture antennas, Receiving antennas. Propagation. Prerequisite: EE 71.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 73
courses.title: Transmission Lines
paras: Circuital aspects of wire transmission lines; steady state and transient analysis. Communication lines. Power lines.
Prerequisite: EE 42, EE 71.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 74
courses.title: Microwave Theory
paras: Review of network theory, General microwave circuit theorems. Waveguide circuit lements. Resonant cavities as circuit elements. Waveguide junctions. Mode transformations. Non-reciprocal microwave components. Microwave antennas.
Prerequisite: EE 72, Math 45.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 75
courses.title: Electric and Magnetic Materials
paras: An introduction to the physical interpretation of the dielectric magnetic and conductive properties of materials; dielectric materials in static and alternating fields; atomic interpretation of magnetic properties; conductivity of metals; the mechanism of conduction in semiconductors; semiconductor rectifiers and transistors.
Prerequisite: ME 31.
3 hours, one term.

courses.label: ECE 81
courses.title: Control Systems I
paras: A study of the controlled utilization of energy in physical systems, Formulation of transfer functions of systems from their physical configuration. Response of systems in the time domain, root-locus analysis, Response of systems in the frequency domain, relation to root locus, Stability considerations, compensation. Prerequisite: EE 42, Math 45.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 82
courses.title: Control Systems II
paras: Further study of feedback control systems, Design of control systems, examples taken from electrical and hydromechanical systems. Analogue computer simulation. Introduction to non-linear systems analysis, phase plane and describing function techniques, Introduction to statistical systems analysis, optimum system criteria, Prerequisite: EE 81. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 83
courses.title: Communication Theory
paras: Relation between information content of messages and system capacity; transmission through electric networks; modulation systems; periodic sampling, noise, comparative analysis of information transmission systems. The role of system bandwidth and noise in limiting the transmission of information is stressed.
Prerequisite: EE 52.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ECE 91
courses.title: Electrical Laboratory I

courses.title: Advanced Network Theory
paras: Study of linear graphs and their associated matrices, graphs of passive and active networks. courses.label: ECE 613

ENGLISH MAJOR IN GENERAL ARTS

In Year I the prospective English major should select English 100, Philosophy 100, Natural Science 100, at least one of French 100, German 100, and Latin 100, and other subjects in accord with the general regulations.

In Year II the English major shall complete English 200 and 250; in the course of Years II and III he shall complete one further Honours English course and at least two of English 210, 220, 225, 230, 330, 335, or any Honours English courses; in Year III he shalt also complete English 345 and shall write a Comprehensive Examination in the general field of English Literature.

Subjects related to the study of English, and from which the English major is expected to choose his optional courses, are the following: Classics, French, German, History (especially English or American), Philosophy, Psychology, Religious Knowledge, Russian, Sociology and Spanish.
Note on numbering: English 100 and 200 are designed for both Honours and General students. Otherwise courses numbered 250-299, 350-399, and 450-499 are Honours
courses, and all others are General courses.

Note on prerequisites: Normally English 100 (or its equivalent at another University) will be prerequisite to all courses numbered 200 and above (except 225 and 235). In addition English 200 (or its equivalent) will normally be prerequisite to English 380, 450, 455, 460 and 470.

courses.label: ENGL 5
courses.title: Expository Writing
paras: Designed for those Engineering students who enter the University from Grade 12, this course seeks to help them gain a reasonable command of written English, and so consists of the discussion of the English language, the reading of expository essays, and the frequent writing of such essays.
Texts: Braddock, Introductory Readings on the English Language; Morrison & Robbins, As A Man Thinks; Kazin, The Open Form; Sears, Harbrace Guide to the Library and the Research Paper. .
3 lectures.

courses.label: ENGL 15
courses.title: English Literature
paras: Designed as an option for first-year Engineering students, this course seeks to further the understanding and appreciation of the various types of English literature and of the humanistic values to be found in it. Since such understanding cannot be separated from the clear and effective communication of the ideas concerned, students are required to write a number of essays on topics related to the literature studied.
Texts: First term: Scott, Topics and Opinions, First Series; Conrad, Lord Fim; Amis, Lucky Fim; Paton, Too Late the Phalarope; Golding, Lord of the Flies.
Second Term: Barnet, Berman & Burto, Eight Great Tragedies, Eight Great Comedies; Coffin, The Major Poets.

courses.title: The Periods of English Literature, I: Mediaeval to Augustan

(For both General and Honours students who are likely to take a further English course.) Texts: The Norton Anthology of English Literature, vol. 1: Shakespeare, Twelfth Night, Othello, A Winter's Tale; oncom, The Alchemist; Defoe, Moll Flanders; Fielding, Joseph Andrews; Swift, Gulliver’s Travels; Thomas, Form and Substance; and further texts to be prescribed by the individual instructors for the introductory part of the course.

courses.label: GEOG 15
courses.title: Survey of Geography
paras: This one term course presents a general review of the field of Geography, its scope, approach, and basic concepts. The primary aim is to provide the student with background, material, readings, sources and ideas against which major political developments, international economic relationships, and current problems of the commonwealth and underveloped areas may be viewed. Course topics include: the development and character of modern Geography; fundamentals of physiography; population patterns and problems; resources, economic growth and industrialization; the geographic bases of political patterns and events; and urban growth and land use planning.
3 lectures, half course.

courses.label: GEOG 100
courses.title: Introductory Physical and Cultural Geography
paras: This course is designed to introduce the student to the field of modern geography, its methods, concepts, materials and point of view. A major part of the course is devoted to a systematic examination of the elements of the natural environment, (including landforms, weather, and climate), and their distribution and significance in the human habitat. Selected aspects of economic and political geography are then considered, with an emphasis on world resources and the geographic bases of economic development, international trade, and political relationships. NOTE: Geography 100, or its equivalent, is normally a prerequisite for other courses in geography.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: GEOG 200
courses.title: Climatology and Meteorology

2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: GEOG 210
courses.title: Geography of World Resources and Industries

2 lectures, 2 hour seminar.

courses.label: GEOG 220
courses.title: World Regional Geography

2 lectures, 2 hours seminar.

courses.label: GEOG 300
courses.title: Geomorphology
paras: Advanced study of the processes of geomorphology. Analysis of the deve opment and distribution of landforms, with emphasis on pleistocene deposits. The relationships between landforms and natural vegetation, climate, soils, water resources, and man’s economic activities.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: GEOG 341

lectures.

courses.label: GEOG 345
courses.title: Political Geography
paras: An examination of the geographic aspects of the world’s political patterns; politico-territorial problems of states; contemporary international problems and their geographic backgrounds; geopolitics.
3 lectures.

courses.label: GEOG 350
courses.title: Urban Geography and Settlement Patterns
paras: A description and analysis of the geographic characteristics and relationships of urban centers, their origin, development, distribution, functions, internal structure, economic and political organization; industrial and commercial locational factors; the effects of transportation on settlement patterns.
2 lectures, 2 hours seminar.

courses.label: GEOG 355

courses.label: MATH 333
courses.title: Differential Equations
paras: First-order differential equations. Linear equations with constant coefficients. Solutions in series. Systems of differential equations. Introduction to partial differential equations. Introduction to integral equations.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 334
courses.title: Numerical Methods
paras: Finite differences. Solution of equations. Computation with series and integrals. Linear systems and matric methods. Difference equations and relaxation methods. Numerical solution of partial differential equations. Methods employing electronic computers. .
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: MATH 335
courses.title: Finite Differences
paras: A theoretical course in the calculus of finite differences to include summation, the differences of zero, numerical integration, the relation betwen integration and summation, An introduction to difference equations.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 336
courses.title: Life Contingencies
paras: An advanced course on problems of single lives. 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 337
courses.title: Advanced Mechanics
paras: Vectorial treatment of physical problems. Special examples from three-dimensional statics and dynamics. Introduction to the Lagrange equations, 2 jJectures.

courses.label: MATH 338
courses.title: Mathematical Statistics
paras: An advanced mathematical course including the multivariate normal law and related distributions. Normal regression theory. Applications to hypothesis testing and analysis of variance.
2 lectures..

courses.label: MATH 339
courses.title: Electromagnetism I
paras: Electrostatics and magnetostatics. The theorem of Gauss. Development of the Maxwell equations. lectures.

courses.label: MATH 430
courses.title: Finite Projective Geometries
paras: Representations by fields, groups, and algebras. Finite Euclidean geometries. Sub-geometries. Collineation groups. Tactical configurations. 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 431
courses.title: Algebra III
paras: A continuation of course 331. 2 lectures. .

courses.label: MATH 432
courses.title: Functions of a Complex Variable
paras: Topological concepts. Analytic continuation. The Riemann surface. Entire meromorphic functions, Periodic functions. Special . functions. General metric spaces. Function spaces. The integral as an operator.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 433
courses.title: Theory of Integration
paras: Measure theory. The Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral. Lebesgue integration. lecture.

courses.label: MATH 434
courses.title: Differential Equations of Mathematical Physics
paras: Boundary-value problems, Orthogonal functions. Bessel functions. The Legendre polynomials. The Fourier integral. The Laplace transform. The wave equation.
2 lectures, 1 hour problems.

courses.label: MATH 435
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Numerical problems arising in actuarial science and statistics. 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: MATH 436
courses.title: Life Contingencies II
paras: An advanced course on the death and survival of multiple lives. 2 lectures.
437; Graduation and Mortality. Methods of constructing and graduating mortality tables. 1 lecture.

courses.label: MATH 438
courses.title: Estimation and Hypothesis Testing
paras: The mathematics and logic of estimation and hypothesis testing. Information. Consistency. Efficiency. Sufficiency. Fiducial and confidence intervals, The problems of large and small samples.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 439
courses.title: Theory of Experimental Design
paras: The logic of experimental designs. Randomization. Experimental and sampling errors. Mathematical methods of constructing various designs. Applications to problems in the sciences.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 440
courses.title: Advanced Probability
paras: Recurrent events. Markov processes and applications to Physics and Biology, including diffusion processes and epidemics. 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 441
courses.title: Quantum Theory
paras: The classical mechanics of Lagrange and Hamilton. Introduction to quantum theory. 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 442
courses.title: Theory of Relativity
paras: Covariant and contravariant tensors. Riemannian space. Gaussian curvature. The Lorentz transformation and Einstein’s special theory. Introduction to the general theory of relativity.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 443
courses.title: Electromagnetism II
paras: Applications of the Maxwell equations. Reflection and refraction. Introduction to wave guides and antennae. 2 lectures.
444, Elasticity. Problems in stress and strain. Isotropic bodies. Equilibrium equations, Torsion and Flexure. 2 lectures.
445, Hydrodynamics. Continuous and discontinuous flow. Aerofoil theory. Viscous flow. 2 lectures.

446, History 01 Mathematics. The development of Mathematics from ancient to modern times, including study of prominent mathematicians and their works, Problems will be worked using both modern and historical approaches.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 447
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Applications of probability theory to theoretical
Physics. 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 448
courses.title: Differential Geometry
paras: Curves in space. Gaussian curvature. Tensorial notation. Introduction to differential manifolds, 2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 449
courses.title: Experimental Design
paras: Logic of experimental designs. Randomization. Experimental and sampling errors. Designs applied in biology. Methods of analysis for pectorial designs, Latin squares, etc.
lectures.

courses.label: MATH 450
courses.title: Applied Analysis
paras: Applied Mathematics for Science majors. Ordinary and partial differential equations. Laplace and Fourier transforms. Special functions. Fourier series. Vector and matric methods. Calculus of variations. Other topics in advanced calculus.
2 lectures.

courses.label: MATH 601
courses.title: Advanced Numerical Analysis
paras: Finite differences, with stress on operator methods and central difference notation. Iterative procedures for solution of equations. Computations involving integrals, Error estimation. Curve fitting and orthogonal polynomials. Gaussian quadrature. Methods of solving ordinary and partial differential equations. Eigenvalue problems for systems of linear equations and for differential equatoins. Matric methods in applied mathematics.

courses.label: MATH 603
courses.title: Gas Dynamics
paras: Concepts from thermodynamics, One-dimensional gas dynamics. One-dimensional wave motion. Waves in supersonic flow. Flow in ducts and wind tunnels. Methods of measurement. Equations of frictionless flow. Small-perturbation theory. Bodies of revolution and slender body theory. The similarity rules of highspeed flow. Transonic flow. The method of characteristics. Effects of viscosity and conductivity. Laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Concepts from gas kinetics.

courses.label: MATH 604
courses.title: Special Functions
paras: Elliptic functions. The hypergeometric function. The gamma and beta functions. The functions of Laplace, Legendre, Lamé, Mathieu, and Bessel. Orthogonal functions; the functions of Laguerre, Hermite, Chebyshev.

courses.label: MATH 611
courses.title: Advanced Probability
paras: Review of classical probability theory, including occupancy problems, the binomial, Poisson, and normal distributions, applications in physics. Recurrent events. Markov chains, stochastic processes, including the ruin problem and diffusion processes; application to information theory, radar, queuing problems, etc.

courses.label: MATH 615
courses.title: Group Characteristics and Representation Theory
paras: 621, Computer Programming. General concepts of computer types and applications. Flow charting. Coding, instruction formats. Editing. Storage elements and buffers. Control and accuracy in digital computers. Input and output devices and their use, Number systems. Automatic programming and universal computer languages. Logic and Boolean Algebra. Heuristic programming. Elements of logical design.

courses.label: MATH 622
courses.title: Vector and Tensor Analysis
paras: Vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, Euclidean spaces, groups of transformations, algebra of tensors; covariant differentiation, divergence, Laplacian, curl. Generalizations to Riemannian spaces. Applications to other fields including differential geometry, mechanics, elasticity, hydrodynamics, electricity, and general relativity.
half course.

courses.label: MATH 631
courses.title: Advanced Computer Techniques
paras: Operational mathematics. Laplace transforms. Computer approximations for algebraic and transcendental functions. Numerical integration. Operations research models. Simplex method of linear programming. Convex programming. Dynamic programming. Monte Carlo techniques. Information theory and transmission. Information retrieval..

courses.label: MATH 641
courses.title: Mathematical Methods of Operations Research
paras: Review of the mathematics used in model making. Methods of optimization, including linear programming and game theory. Applications to business, industrial, and military problems, including inventory replacement and allocaticn models, queuing theory, and decision theory.

courses.label: MATH 655
courses.title: Combinatorial Analysis
paras: 664, Calculus of Variations. The Euler equations and the Legendre and Jacobi conditions. The Weierstrass E function and sufficient conditions. The theory of trans-
versals and the isoperimetric problems. Hilbert’s existence theorem. Selected topics from the theories of Kneser and,Caratheodory; the problem of Bolza.

courses.label: MATH 675
courses.title: Linear Graphs
paras: -Definitions and[basic theorems. Planar graphs and Kuratowski’s Theorem. Selected topics from*advanced graph theory.
