11, Dynamics. An extension of the physics course in Mechanics with particular reference to engineering situations and problems for Civil and Electrical Engineering students. The vector treatment of dynamics is used. Relative motion, integration of Newton’s Law for rectlinear translation, energy methods, methods of momentum. 2 lectures, one term. . .

courses.label: ME 12
courses.title: Dynamics
paras: An introduction to the kinematics of particle and rigid body motion. Elementary vector mathematics. Impulse-momentum equations. Work-energy meth.
ods and Euler’s equations. Simple gyroscopes, central force motions. 3 lectures, 2 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 13
courses.title: Kinematics
paras: A basic course in kinematics emphasizing the creative approach. Uniform rotary motion including rolling cylinders, gears and the synthesis of gear trains including planetaries. Non-uniform motion including cams, gears and linkages. Programming non-uniform motion and the synthesis of cam mechanisms, non-circular gear trains and linkages, . “ 2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory, one term.

21, Mechanics of Machinery. The effects of dynamic forces in machines. Introduction to mechanical vibrations, Transient forces. Static force analysis, dynamic force analysis, balancing, cam dynamics, dynamics of feedback systems.
Prerequisites: ME 13. 2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 22
courses.title: Design of Machines
paras: Theory and application of mechanics of solids to machine parts. Design of machine elements; power screws, shafting, bearings, belts, gears, flywheels, clutches and brakes, crankshafts, springs, thin and thick wall pressure vessels, lubrication, ball and roller bearings.
Prerequisites: ME 21.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 23
courses.title: Analysis and Synthesis of Machines
paras: Principle of optimum design, optimizing for minimum cost, maximum power capability, minimum weight, effects of manufacturing errors on product performance, statistical consideration for the factor of safety, optimum design of machine elements; torsion shafts, beams, gears, etc. Castigliano’s theorem, fluctuating loads, impact forces, axially symmetric stress conditions, Bearing design.
Prerequisites: ME 22.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 25
courses.title: Mechanical Vibrations
paras: A broad development of mechanical vibration and impact. Transient phenomena, self-excited vibration, torsional oscillations, multimass systems, electromechanical systems and analogies. Forced vibrations, elimination and absorption of vibration. Measurement of vibration.
Prerequisites: ME 21.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 31
courses.title: Properties of Materials
paras: Physico-chemical foundations: review of the atomic, molecular, crystal, and grain structures. Effect of microstructures on mechanical Properties of metallic, ceramic, and organic materials. Principles of mechanical, thermal, and electromagnetic properties.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 32
courses.title: Materials Science I
paras: The arrangement of atoms in solid materials. Crystallography and x-ray analysis. Theory of dislocations and other imperfections in crystalline structures. Equilibrium relationships in multi-phase materials. Phase rule and phase diagrams.
Prerequisites: Phys. 15
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 33
courses.title: Materials Science II
paras: Properties of metallic phases. Equilibrium and nonequilibrium relationships in steels. Ferrous and non-ferrous alloys. Properties and structure of ceramic and organic materials. Corrosion, electrical and magnetic properties. Irradiation of materials.
Prerequisites: ME 32.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 34
courses.title: Solid State for Engineers
paras: Quantitative analysis of energy states in solids. Transformation rates. Bonding energies in metallic, covalent, ionic and molecular solids. Theories of mechanical, thermal, electrical, and magnetic properties. Optical and surface phenomena.
Prerequisites: ME 33.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 35
courses.title: Nuclear Engineering
paras: An introductory course in nuclear reactor theory and design, isotope applications and fusion. Topics covered will include fission and the chain reaction, reactor principles, reactor components and materials, heat transfer, reactor design, uses of isotopes, applications of nuclear power and the fusion process. Prerequisites: Math 31, Phys 15.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 36
courses.title: Physical Metallurgy
paras: Review of atomic and crystal structures. Theory of solidification of metals. Elasticity and plasticity of metals. Corrosion and diffusion. Properties of engineering alloys.
Prerequisites: Chem. 11, Phys 15.
3 lectures, one term.
37, Ceramics. The crystallography of ionic and co-valent compounds. A study of the mechanical properties of single crystals and polycrystals. Properties of special ceramic materials.
Prerequisite: Chem 11, Phys 15.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 41
courses.title: Manufacturing Analysis
paras: Analysis of industry as a communication system, production system and financial system. Work flow as related to physical facilities, plant layout, and product design. Basic manufacturing processes as related to statistical matching of physical properties of materials and performance characteristics of machinery.
3 lectures, one term.
42, Industrial Organization. Principles and forms of organization, industrial

functions and types of industry. Industrial economic studies and controls. Information athering and information analysis, decision making and information dissemenation. roduction inventory, quality, cost, and budgetary controls.
Prerequisites: ME 41, Math 3)
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 51
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: Primarily intended for electrical engineering students, this course is an introduction to thermodynamics and heat transfer. Topics covered include: concepts of property, state, equilibrium, heat, and work; equations of state; zeroth, first, and second laws; entropy; conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. Applications to selected thermodynamic systems of interest to electrical engineers. 3 Tectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 52
courses.title: Thermodynamics I
paras: Concepts of property, state, equilibrium, and temperature. Heat and work. The first and second laws, Entropy. Equations of state. Availability, irreversibility, and efficiency. Chemical reactions. Applications to the analysis of engineering systems.
Prerequisites: Math 22.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 53
courses.title: Heat Transfer
paras: Steady and unsteady state conduction; natural and forced convection; heat transfer by radiation. Heat exchanger design and analysis. Heat transfer in high speed flow. Mass transfer.
Prerequisites: ME 52, Math 31.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

54, Thermodynamics II. Review of the basic concepts and postulates of thermodynamics and the conditions for equilibrium. Reactive systems. An introduction to irreversible thermodynamics. Applications to selected engineering systems including direct conversion devices, gas turbines, Advanced topics in heat transfer. Prerequisites: ME 52.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 55
courses.title: Statistical Thermodynamics
paras: Entropy and information. The formalism of statistical mechanics. The perfect monotomic gas. The general concept of temperature. Macroscopic properties of closed systems. Perfect diatomic gases and crystals. Properties of non-perfect gases, liquids, and solids. Generalized PVT data. Open systems. The grand potential function and the general criterion for equilibrium. Chemically reactive systems. Solutions and heterogeneous systems. Variables other than ressure. Inherently irreversible processes. rerequisites: Math 55. 3 lectures, one term. .

courses.label: ME 56
courses.title: Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transfer
paras: Heat transfer in turbulent flows. Reynolds’ analogy. Boiling and condensation. Heat and momentum transfer in highvelocity flows and rarefied gases. Radiation heat transfer. Mass transfer in laminar and turbulent flows. Analogue methods, Introductory kinetic theory of transport properties.
Prerequisite: ME 53.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 61
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
paras: Fluid statics, basic equations of fluid flow, viscous effects and fluid resistance, dimensional analysis and dynamic similitude. Compressible flow, two-dimensional ideal fluid flow, turbomachinery, flow measuring techniques, pipe and open channel flow, automatic fluid controls, hydraulic systems.
Prerequisites: ME 12, Math 31..
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

62: Fluid Dynamics, Introduction to the concepts, principles, and methods of fluid dynamics. Fundamental equations of fluid motion. Stream function and velocity potential. Fluid flow over simple bodies. Airfoils in two and three-dimensional flows. Viscosity effects: boundary layer, turbulence and drag. Lift.
Prerequisites: ME 61, Math 44.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 63
courses.title: Fluid Machinery
paras: Application of the principles of subsonic flow. Mechan-
isms of mass and energy transfer in Fluid Machinery. Dimensional analysis and per-
formance characteristics of turbo-machinery. Special treatment of displacement and
centrifugal pumps, blowers, fans, hydraulic turbines, torque converters, fluid coulings; and: propellers. Introduction to fluid power transmission and control systems. rerequisites: ME 61..
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 64
courses.title: Hydraulic Engineering
paras: A senior course in the application of fundamentals studied in ME 61. Fans, pumps, compressors, turbines, fluid couplings, back water computations; hydraulic jump, water hammer, hydrology. Power hydraulics and control hydraulics. Application of theory and techniques to engineering problems. Prerequisites: ME 61. ..
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 65
courses.title: Gasdynamics
paras: Foundations of fluid dynamics and themodynamics. The introductory concepts of compressible fluid flow. Isentropic flow behaviour; normal and oblique shock waves: Flow in constant area ducts with friction and heat transfer. Generalized one-dimensional continuous flow.
Prerequisites: ME 53, ME 61.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: ME 71
courses.title: Fundamentals of Design
paras: Principles of information gathering, analysis, hypothesis creation, hypothesis testing, and solution communication. Discussions of design as environmentally controlled man-machine systems. Discussion of the relationships between the.technical, and non-technical aspects of design. Exercises and applications of the above concepts.
1 lecture, 2 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 72
courses.title: Professional Creativity
paras: A continuation of ME 71 Fundamentals of Design, into the following areas: discussion of the psychological aspects of creativity; judgment, environment, fixations, and reflection. The role of techniques; technique grouping. Knowledge; sources and skills, evolution of perspective. Planning and plans; statistical dependability, role of schedules, series and parallel actions. Establishing measures; ambiquity, inference, analogy and model measurements, Optimizing structures; role of detail, conflict situations, error and balance measurements. Information transfer; sense filters, ‘noise’, language and symbology.
Prerequisites: ME 71.
3 lectures, 2 hours laboratory, one term.

1 hour, one term..

courses.label: ME 82
courses.title: Mechanical Engineering Projects
paras: Engineering assignments requiring the student to demonstrate initiative and assume responsibility. Student activity is guided and co-ordinated by faculty supervisors. In selecting and assigning projects, particular account is taken of the student’s field of specialization. Projects, in general, involve technical disciplines beyond the strictly mechanical engineering field.
9 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: ME 601
courses.title: Aerodynamics of Compressible Fluids
paras: Two-dimensional subsonic flow with small perturbations; hodograph and other methods of solution. Three-dimensional subsonic flow. Two-dimensional supersonic flow with small perturbations; the method of characteristics. Oblique shocks. Axially symmetric supresonic flow. Supersonic wing theory. Hypersonic flow.
one term.

courses.label: ME 602
courses.title: Fluid Machinery II
paras: Thermodynamics and fluid mechanics for flow phenomena in steam and gas turbines, air compressors, and jet propulsion devices. Operating characteristics of fluid machinery involving compressible flow. Selected problems of mechanical strength and vibrations encountered in rotating machinery and blading. one term.

courses.label: ME 605
courses.title: Kinematics II
paras: An extension of ME 13. Computing mechanisms, space mechanisms. Use of computers in synthesis and analysis. Four-bar linkage, coupler curves, path curvature. Euler-Savory equation, polode curvature. Numerical and graphical methods. Five-bar linkages.
one term.

courses.label: ME 606
courses.title: Hypersonic Aerodynamics
paras: Fundamental concepts of hypersonic flow. Twoand three-dimensional hypersonic flow. Hypersonic small-disturbance theory. Slender body theory. Minimum drag bodies. Hypersonic flow over blunt bodies. Stability and control of hypersonic vehicles. Real gas effects.
one term.

courses.label: ME 607
courses.title: Transport Phenomena
paras: Viscosity and the mechanism of momentum transport. Velocity distributions in laminar and turbulent flow. The equations of change and interphase transport in isothermal systems. Temperature distributions and energy transport in laminar and turbulent flows. Energy transport by radiation. Diffusivity and the mechanism of mass transport. Concentration distributions in laminar and tur. bulent flow. Interphase transport in multicomponent systems. Evaluation of transport coefficients.
one term.

courses.label: ME 608
courses.title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics
paras: Review of general concepts and basic relations. Solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations for viscous flow. Laminar and turbulent boundary layers flow for incompressible and compressible fluids. Selected topics in two-dimensional incompressible flow of a frictionless fluid. Three-dimensional incompressible flow.
one term.

courses.label: ME 609
courses.title: Mechanics of Viscous Flow
paras: The formulation and properties of the Navier- Stokes equations.and some exact solutions, Boundary layer concepts and the Prandtl equations for two-dimensional flow. Similarity solutions, Exact and approximate solutions. Axially symmetrical and unsteading boundary layers, boundary layer control. Laminar stability and transition to turbulence.
one term.

courses.label: ME 611
courses.title: Conduction Heat Transfer
paras: Steady conduction in isotropic media. Unsteady heat conduction in fixed isotropic media. Heat conduction with phase change and moving boundaries. Conduction in flowing media with and without mass transfer. Conduction in anisotropic media.
one term.

courses.label: ME 612
courses.title: Radiation Heat Transfer I
paras: Fundamentals of radiation. Determination of radiation properties. Analysis of radiation heat transfer. Solar, terrestrial and planetary radiation, Temperature control of satellites and space vehicles. Solar power plants for space vehicles. Direct solar energy conversion systems.
one term.

courses.label: ME 613
courses.title: Radiation Heat Transfer II
paras: Summary of radiation between surfaces, view factors, emissivity measurements. Flame radiation, radiation from clouds of luminous particles, Gas radiation, calculation of flame emissivities based on flame spectroscopy. Optical temperature measurement.
one term.

614, Combustion Science. Brief survey of combustion thermodynamics. Combustion of premixed gases, laminar and turbulent flames. Detonations. Combustion in flow systems. Laminar and turbulent diffusion flames. Combustion of liquid and solid fuels. Ignition and flame spread. Combustion in I-C engines, furnaces, rocket motors.
one term.

615, Fundamentals of Aerodynamic Heating. Basic equations and properties of laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Skin friction and heat transfer. Predictions by approximate methods, Basic parameter for low density flow. Slip and free-molecule flow. Stagnation point heat transfer. Mass transfer cooling.
one term.

courses.label: ME 621
courses.title: Survey of Space Technology
paras: Brief survey of propulsion, celestial mechanics.
astronomy and astrophysics of the solar system. Energy conversion in space. Electric
propulsion and fundamentals of magnetohydrodynamics. Re-entry dynamics, ablative eat protection, trajectory analysis, Optimum thrust and steering programmes. Lunar
trip. Summary of experimental results on geophysics, cosmic radiation, the earth’s
atmosphere. Materials for space.
one term.

courses.label: ME 631
courses.title: Fluid Power Control
paras: Fundamentals of fluid flow. Fluid power conversion in positive displacement. Pumps and motors, performance characteristics. Energy storage in working fluids, unsteady flow with elastic-energy storage. Fluid power transmission: dynamic response characteristics. Hydraulic and pneumatic control valve configurations, Dynamic interaction in hydraulic, pneumatic, and electric control systems, Valve instability and non-linear effects in hydraulic systems with inertia loading.
one term.

courses.label: ME 641
courses.title: Theory of Metallic Materials
paras: Bond theory, Fermi levels, dia-para and ferromagnetism. Theoretical and experimental studies of dislocations. Structure and behaviour of polycrystalline metals.
one term.

courses.label: ME 642
courses.title: Behaviour of Materials
paras: Review of basic crystallography. Dislocation theory with special reference to non-metallic substances. Properties and influence of point defects. Ductility, fatigue and fracture phenomena, Surface effects. Mechanical properties of special single crystal forms, polycrystals and poly-phase materials.
one term.

courses.label: ME 698
courses.title: Special Directed Studies
paras: one term.

courses.label: PHIL 100J
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
paras: A study of St. Thomas and his writings; fundamental Thomistic principles. ours.

courses.label: PHIL 140J
courses.title: Logic and Epistemology
paras: Nature and division of philosophy; nature of logic, the term; the proposition; argumentation; induction and deduction; scientific demonstration. Truth; certitide; evidence; sense and intellectual knowledge; criterion of truth; contemporary theories.
3 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 200A
courses.title: History of Philosophy I
paras: A preliminary examination of the philosophy of Plato. Mention will be made of the historical Socrates and some of the Presocratics, Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
3 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 200B
courses.title: History of Philosophy III, A preliminary account of early modern philosophies, with emphasis on the views of Descartes, Locke, Malebranche, Leibnitz, Spinoza, Berkeley, Hume
paras: Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
3 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 200J
courses.title: Cosmology and Philosophy of Science
paras: Corporal bodies and change; quantitative and qualitative characteristics; motion; time, space; hylomorphic theory. Nature of science; abstraction; necessity; foundation and object of science; scientific method; hypothesis and theory.
ours.

courses.label: PHIL 210A
courses.title: History of Philosophyjli
paras: A preliminary examination of the philosophy of Aristotle, particularly with reference to his Metaphysics, Physics and Psychology, a preliminary examination of Mediaeval philosophy.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 100, 3 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 210B
courses.title: Moral Philosophy
paras: The various alternative ways of dealing theoretically with questions about human moral value. Some of the views of the following positions will be discussed: the Epicureans, the Stoics, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Christianity, Spinoza, the Utilitarians, Nietzsche, Schopenhaur, Shaftesbury. Emphasis will be placed on relating these various views to the ethical pronouncements of the modern social sciences particularly cultural anthropology, behaviourism and Freud. Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
3 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 220
courses.title: Logic, Introductory and Intermediate
paras: Various systems of deductive logic. Inductive logic and scientific method. As compared to the elementary logic, contained in Philosophy 100 the treatment here will be more extensive and lay greater emphasis on the attaining of technical facility. This course may be taken without Philosophy 100 as a prerequisite but may be taken subsequent to Philosophy 100 without fear of redundancy.
3 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 240J
courses.title: Ethics
paras: End of Man; the human act; law, conscience; morality; rights and duties; duties of man as an individual and as a member of society. ours.

courses.label: PHIL 250
courses.title: Tutorial for Honours
paras: 1 hour.

courses.label: PHIL 300A
courses.title: History of Philosophy IV
paras: The Philosophy of Kant. Emphasis will be placed on the Prolegomena, some sections of the Critique of Pure Reason.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 200.
3 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 300B
courses.title: History of Philosophy V
paras: From Hegel to the Present. The course will include a survey of 19th and 20th century idealism, pragmatism, and modern empiricist, analyst, linguistic and positivist schools including such philosophers as Bertrand Russell, A. J. Ayer, H. H. Brice, and Wittgenstein.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 300a.
3 hours, half course. |

courses.label: PHIL 300J
courses.title: Metaphysics and Natural Theology
paras: The notion and analogy of being; the primary principles of being; the properties, division, and causes of being. Demonstration of existence of God; His nature and attributes; the divine intelligence and will; creation and providence.
3 hours. ©

courses.label: PHIL 310
courses.title: Twentieth Century Moral and Theological Views
paras: A sequel to the course on Moral Philosophy in which similar topics are dealt with in the form in which they have appeared in contemporary writing and discussions. Prerequisite: Philosophy 210.
ours.

courses.label: PHIL 315
courses.title: Political Philosophy
paras: Philosophical analysis of central concepts in political theory. The effect of the central issues of moral Philosophy, epistemology, and metaphysics on the formation of political theories. Examples will be drawn from the work of philosophers of a number of periods and schools—for example, Plato, Aritsotle, St. Thomas Aquinas, Hobbes, Locke, Hegel, Marx and contemporary thinkers. Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
ours.

courses.label: PHIL 320
courses.title: Introduction to Aesthetics
paras: The philosophical consideration of art and beauty. A study of the basic problems with examples from historical and contemporary writers. Various theories of art criticism and literary criticism. Art related to society, morality, the sciences and religion. . Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 330A
courses.title: Oriental Philosophy
paras: A survey of non-western philosophy, particularly that of China, Japan, and India. The views of such philosophers as Confucius, Lao-Tze and Mencius will be discussed and the philosophical content of the early Hindu and Buddhist writings examined. Zen Buddhism and other modern views.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 100..
2 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 330B
courses.title: Philosophy of History
paras: Consideration of the various possible views about the ultimate nature and significance of history and historical knowledge. Such views as the following are examined: St. Augustine, Vico, Hegel, Marx, Spengler, Croce, Collingwood and Toynbee.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 100.
2 hours, half course.

courses.label: PHIL 340
courses.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
paras: Specific problems regarding the philosophical underpinnings of various sciences and disciplines, including Physics, Biology, Mathematics, Psychology, History, Political Science and Economics, English and other literatures. Conducted by one philosophy instructor in conjunction with one other “visiting” instructor from the discipline concerned. Normal period for each discipline will be two weeks..
Prerequisite: Two full courses in Philosophy.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 340J
courses.title: History of Philosophy
paras: A survey of Philosophy from Presocratics to contemporary philosophers. 3 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 348J
courses.title: Seminar in Philosophy
paras: A special study of the principal philosophers of the modern and contemporary eras. ours.
$9. Senior Essay. For Philosophy majors in the pass course. 1 hour.

courses.label: PHIL 450
courses.title: Epistemology
paras: The basic problems in the theory of knowledge, the nature of logical inference, concepts, causal and rational necessity, determinism, freedom, meaning, language, the fundamental nature of communication. Prerequisite: Philosophy 300a.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 451
courses.title: The Central Problems in Aesthetics
paras: The relation of the phenomena peculiar to aesthetic experience to cognitive grounds. The ontological and epistemological status of the passions and the individual quale of a work of art. Prerequisite: hilosophy 300a, 320.
ours.

courses.label: PHIL 453
courses.title: Mediaeval Philosophy
paras: Detailed consideration of selected portions of the works of St. Thomas and other mediaeval philosophers such as Occam, St. Anselm, Albertus Magnus, St. Bernard, Duns Scotus. .
Prerequisite: Philosophy 200a.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 452
courses.title: Ancient Philosophy
paras: Detailed consideration of selected portions of the works of Plato and Aristotle, Suggested Works: Plato’s Timaeus, Theaetetus and Philebus. Aristotle’s Metaphysics.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 200a, 210a.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 454
courses.title: Continental Rationalism
paras: The Philosophy of Descartes, Leibnitz and pinoza.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 210a, 300a.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 455
courses.title: The Philosophy of Kant
paras: The Critique of Pure Reason. Selected passages of the Critique of Judgment.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 300a.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 456
courses.title: Existential Philosophy and Phenomenology
paras: A study of selected readings. Prerequisite: Philosophy 300. With the consent of the instructor, this course is also open to general students with two full courses in philosophy.
ours.
457, Metaphysics. Theories of reality including study of such fundamental concepts as being, form, substance, causality, process, universal, and particular.
Prerequisite: Philosophy 300.
2 hours.

courses.label: PHIL 460
courses.title: Problems
paras: Seminar projects not readily classifiable into the above categories. Prerequisite: Philosophy 300. 2jhours.

paras: 1 hour.

paras: 1 hour.

paras: Fundamentals of modern physics: special theory of relativity, quantization of electromagnetic radiation, wave properties of particles, the hydrogen atom, atomic and X-ray spectra, nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, molecular and solid state physics.

courses.label: PHYS 402
courses.title: X-ray and Spectrographic Analysis
paras: Crystallography, production and properties of X-rays, X-ray diffraction theory, photographic and spectrometric powder techniques, interpretation of powder diffraction data, applications of polycrystalline diffraction, X-ray fluorescence analysis, electron probe analysis. paras: Atomic and nuclear structure, time dependence of radioactive decay, nuclear radiation—a study of nuclear decay by alpha, beta, gamma, neutron, proton, and deuteron emission, interaction of these particles with matter and their detection, neutron physics, fission, nuclear reactions and the complex nucleus, nuclear forces, nuclear models, new particles.

courses.label: PHYS 404
courses.title: Theoretical Mechanics
paras: Fundamental ideas of analytical mechanics, generalized co-ordinates, Lagrange’s formulation, applications of Lagrange’s equations, Hamilton’s formulation, co-ordinate transformations, the special theory of relativity. 2 lectures, 2 hours problems, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 431
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: Variational principles in mechanics; Hamilton’s formulation of mechanics. Classical theory of small vibrations. Physical principles of the quantum theory; Schroedinger’s wave mechanics; angular momentum operators; the hydrogen atom; perturbation theory.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 432
courses.title: Advanced Electronics
paras: Precision electrical measurements, special purpose tubes and solid state devices, high frequency electronics, pulse and digital circuits, stabilization techniques.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 433
courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in atomic and nuclear physics, solid state physics, and thermodynamics; electrical and electronic measurements; vacuum techniques. In addition, a short research problem will be assigned.
3, 6 or 9 hours laboratory.

courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics H. Identical particles, the exclusion principle, many-electron atoms, X-rays, nuclear particles, nuclear reactions, instruments
paras: 2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 435
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Electronic structure of atoms; atomic spectra; spectroscopic methods; atomic bonding; crystal structure and space lattices; symmetry; crystal geometry; X-ray diffraction theory and methods; crystal formation; defects; physical properties of crystals; free electron theory of metals; band theory of metals and semi-conductors. . .
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, alternate weeks, for students not taking Physics 433 (Advanced Lab.)

courses.label: PHYS 436
courses.title: Physical Mathematics II
paras: Theory of functions of a complex variable. Boundary value problems in mathematical physics. The Fourier integral; Fourier and Laplace transforms. Review of matrix algebra; linear vector spaces; mathematical foundations of the quantum theory. Introduction to group theory. Statistical treatment of experimental data.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 437
courses.title: Topics in Theoretical Physics
paras: Selected subjects for advanced study. 2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 438
courses.title: Geophysics II
paras: A more advanced discussion of seismology and the internal constitution of the Earth, mechanical properties of the Earth’s interior, figure of the Earth and its gravitational field, temperature and thermal history of the Earth, internal magnetic field of the Earth and its electrical properties at depth, the rotation of the Earth and its geophysical effects.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 439
courses.title: The History and Philosophy of Science
paras: The nature of science; science and technology in Egypt and Babylon. The development of science in Greece; the Orphic mysteries and the Jonian philosophers. Plato and Aristotle; Archimedes. The Alexandrian school and the separation of science and philosophy. Technology under the Roman Empire. The mediaeval attitude toward science. The Renaissance. Copernicus and Galileo. Sir Isaac Newton. The physical and biological sciences during the 18th century. Developments during the 19th century in Physics, Chemistry, Technology, Geology. Evolution, and the rise of modern Genetics, The 20th century revolution in pure science and technology.
2 lectures.

2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 442
courses.title: Metal Physics
paras: The course will provide explanations of the physical properties and behaviour of metals and alloys from the viewpoint of atomic physics. Topics included are: solidification of pure metals, perfect and imperfect crystals, alloys, phase diagrams, diffusion, solid state phase transformations, the iron-carbon system, physical properties of metal crystals, elastic and plastic deformation, twinning, radiation damage, recovery and recrystallization, creep, fatigue, fracture, internal friction, free electron and zone theories of metals, electrical, thermal and magnetic properties. 2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 501
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
paras: A review of the laws of electricity and magnetism which form the basis for Maxwell’s equations. Solutions of Maxwell’s equations in free space and subject to various boundary conditions, transmission line theory, radiation and antenna theory, ionosphere propagation.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 503
courses.title: Physics of Solids and Fluids
paras: Vectors and Cartesian tensors. Vector operator calculus. Analysis of stress. Equations of motion. Analysis of deformation and flow. Equation of continuity. Rheological models. Linear theory of elasticity. Bending and torsion of beams. Hydrodynamics of Newtonian viscous fluids.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 504
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: An outline of the modern theory of solids. Atomic bonding and classification of solids, lattice defects in crystals, elastic and plastic deformation of crystals, polycrystalline solids, mechanical and thermal properties of solids, electron and zone theories of solids, electrical, electronic, magnetic and optical properties of solids. Alloys, equilibrium diagrams, phase changes and diffusion in metals.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PHYS 505
courses.title: Seminar and Problem
paras: Each student will prepare and present at least one paper on a technical subject related to his studies, Specific problems may be assigned for investigation and report.
4 hours.

courses.label: PHYS 506
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: Origins of quantum theory. Waves and particles. Wave functions and wave packets. Schroedinger’s equation. One-dimensional motion in regions of varying potential, Fourier analysis, eigenvalues and expectation values. Axiomatic foundations of quantum mechanics. Operators. Angular momentum. Central force systems, hydrogen atom.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 601
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: Principles of the quantum theory. Schroedinger’s equation. The linear oscillator. Angular momentum. The Hydrogen atom. Matrix mechanics, Identical particles and spin, atoms and molecules. Perturbation theory. The semi-classical treatment of radiation. Scattering theory. The Dirac equation.

courses.label: PHYS 602
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
paras: Generalized solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Radiation from a moving charge and from given current distributions. Aperture radiation, electromagnetic horns, diffraction. The latter part of the course will treat selected topics.

courses.label: PHYS 603
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Crystal symmetry and bulk properties; binding energy; defects and their effect on diffusion, deformation, and optical properties; one-electron theory of solids; phonons and specific heat; transport processes and the electronphonon interaction.

courses.label: PHYS 604
courses.title: Advanced Classical Mechanics
paras: Review of elementary mechanics, Lagrangian formulation, variational principles, Hamiltonian formulations; rigid body kinematics and dynamics, special relativity, transformation theory, Hamilton-Jacobi theory.

courses.label: PHYS 605
courses.title: Atomic and Molecular Spectra
paras: One or other of these courses may be offered each year. (a) The spectra emitted by atoms are treated on the basis of the vector model of the atom, as constructed from classical quantum theory and wave. mechanics. Topics include: the Bohr-Sommerfeld model and wave mechanics of the hydrogen atom, the Schroedinger model of the alkali-like atoms with penetrating orbits, fine structure, hyperfine structure, the many electron model and exchange energy, Zeeman effect, jection rules and intensities of emitted radiation. (b) Emission and absorption of radiation by molecules. Topics include: rotational, vibrational and electronic spectra of diatomic molecules, the interaction of vibration and rotation and the finer details of infra-red and Raman spectra, electronic bands, dissociation, polyatomic molecules, intensities and selection rules of transitions.

courses.label: PHYS 607
courses.title: Nuclear Physics
paras: Nuclear size and mass. Semi-emperical mass formula, binding energy and stability, Nuclear forces and scattering between nucleons. Models of the nucleus: shell model, liquid drop model and collective model. Nuclear reactions and conservation laws. 4 and 6 decay.

courses.label: PHYS 608
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Review of essential classical and quantum mechanics; ensembles, microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical; quantum statistical mechanics, theory of the density matrix; applications, mainly in solid state physics.
one term.

courses.label: PHYS 609
courses.title: Topics in Advanced Quantum Mechanics, One or more of the following courses may be offered, but not all will be available in any given year
paras: Course 601 is
a prerequisite.

(a) The Principles of Quantum Mechanics, The nature of quantum physics is demonstrated{more directly by Dirac’s symbolic method than by the usual historical method of presentation based’on Schroedinger and Heisenberg mechanics. This course is an examination of the fundamental theoretical principles of the quantum theory, from the symbolic viewpoint.

(b) Group Theory and Quantum Mechanics. Introduction to group theory: groups, representations of groups, character tables. Group theory and quantum mechanics, the permutation and rotation groups. Applications of the theory to atomic spectra, the theory of angular momentum, molecular symmetry and solid state physics.

(c) Advanced Quantum Mechanics. Dirac theory; the single particle description of relativistic quantum mechanics; bound state and scattering problems—the need for a many-particle (field) approach. Classical relativistic field theory, Feynman-Schwinger quantization of this theory. The radiation field, the electron field, interaction of these fields. The S-matrix; Compton scattering, Coulomb scattering. The magnetic moment of the electron, the Lamb shift. Renormalization.

courses.label: PHYS 610
courses.title: Electron Diffraction
paras: General theory of the diffraction of waves by crystals, experimental technique of electron diffraction, kinematic theory and interprctation of electron diffraction patterns, refraction of electron waves, atomic scattering, dynamical theory, electron interference effects in electron microscope images.

courses.label: PHYS 611
courses.title: Electron Optics and Electron Microscopy
paras: Electrons in electro-static fields, the electrostatic lens, the magnetic lens, aberrations, the electron microscope, electron specimen interactions, Fresnel diffraction and image contour phenomena, electron diffraction and dark-field microscopy, experimental methods in electron microscopy.

courses.label: PHYS 612
courses.title: Low Temperature Physics
paras: Production and measurement of very low temperatures. Low temperature materials and techniques. Thermal, magnetic and electrical properties of matter at very low temperatures. Superconductivity. Liquid helium.

courses.label: PHYS 613
courses.title: Selected Topics in Solid State Physics
paras: One or two of the following topics
may be offered each year.

(a) Imperfections in Crystals. Perfect and imperfect crystals, general properties of point defects and dislocations, interactions of imperfections, solid state phase transformation, plastic deformation and work-hardening of metals, grain boundaries, influence of lattice imperfections on physical properties, internal friction in metals, diffusion, physical observation of lattice defects, generation and annealing of point defects, radiation damage.

(b) Yonic Crystals and Luminescence. The crystalline state — diffraction of X-rays, neutrons, electrons. Classification of solids. Lattice energy of ionic crystals — conductivity and diffusion. Band structure and electron distribution. Electronic and optical properties of alkali halides. (Photo-conductivity and luminescence.)

(c) Inert Gas Solids. Theory of crystal lattices: quantum mechanical basis, interatomic potentials, stability, dynamics of cubic close-packed lattices, thermodynamics of ideal crystals, anharmonicity. Experimental properties.

(d) Advanced Quantum Theory of Solids. Theoretical and experimental techniques for determination of the band structure of metals and semiconductors; electrical and thermal conduction processes and electron-lattice interactions.

courses.label: PHYS 614
courses.title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
paras: Selected topics in theoretical geophysics; seismology, rheology of the Earth, geomagnetism, the Earth’s rotation.

courses.label: PHYS 615
courses.title: General Relativity and Cosmology
paras: Tensor analysis: covariant and contravariant tensors, covariant differentiation, Riemannian space, geodesics, Ricci tensor, Christoffel symbols. General relativity: gravitation and special relativity, equivalence principle, field equations of general relativity, Schwarzschild metric, observational evidence for the general theory. Cosmology: Newtonian, Einstein and de Sitter universes, the expanding universe, cosmological principle and steady-state universe, observational clues.

courses.label: PHYS 616
courses.title: Biophysics
paras: The behaviour of some physical systems encountered in living organisms, Simple cell models: the cell membrane, diffusion problems, respiration, motion, instability and cell division, radiation damage. Specialized cells and organs: the nerve impulse and its propagation, muscle contraction, the red blood corpuscle, haemodynamics, selective filtration of ions, sensory transducers, temperature regulation, the central nervous system.

courses.label: EARTH 130
courses.title: Introductory Geology
paras: Minerals and rocks; geological processes and their effects; structural geology; applications of geology; historical geology; mineral and rock specimens; interpretation of geological and topographical maps; field trips.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.title: Physics and Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the principles of physics and chemistry with emphasis on the historical development of scientific concepts and their significance both to our understanding of the physical universe and to contemporary society.

The extent of the universe, motion, causes of motion, energy; properties of matter, states of matter, basic chemistry, the periodic table; electricity, currents, fields, magnetism; radiation, optics, atomic structure, subatomic chemistry, chemical forces, organic chemistry.

Illustrations of basic principles will be taken from biochemistry, biophysics, geology, and astronomy. The laboratory part of the course is designed to show how scientists gain new knowledge and to point out the difficulties inherent in the use of apparatus. 3 lectures, 2 hours laboratory, alternate weeks.

Psychology 100, or its equivalent, is a prerequisite for all other courses in psychology. For courses at the 300 level, students will normally be expected to have had at least one course in psychology at the 200 level.
Courses at the 400 level are open only to honours students, or students qualifying for a graduate degree, who have an adequate background in psychology.

courses.label: PSYCH 15
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: A short introduction to the methodology and basic principles of some of the major areas of modern psychology such as learning, emotion, perception, and individual differences. (For Engineering students only.)
3 lectures, half course.

courses.label: PSYCH 100
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: This course is deisgned to provide the students with an understanding of the basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioral science. The development of behavior, learning, motivation, emotion, sensation and perception, and individual differences will be studied with reference to the physiological correlates and to environmental factors.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 100J
courses.title: General Psychology
paras: Nature of psychology; organic life, sensory life and its philosophy; intellectual life and its philosophy. lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 210
courses.title: Development and Behavior
paras: The genesis and development of behavior of the human will be traced from conception to maturity. Physiological changes, and socializing processes will be considered in relation to the development of sensory, motor, symbolic and emotional processes. The nature and development of social behavior and personality will also be studied.
lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 220
courses.title: Principles of Learning
paras: This course is designed to introduce the student to learning theory and also to provide an understanding of experimental techniques in this area. The nature of learning will be considered from the establishment of conditioned responses to the development of complex skills. Theories of learning will be critically examined and the application of research findings to the improvement of learning skills will be considered. Laboratory sessions will demonstrate various aspects of learning.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 230
courses.title: Physiological and Comparative Psychology
paras: A study in the relationship between patterns of behavior and physiological processes with comparisons along the phylogenetic scale from infrahuman species to man.
lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 236J
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
paras: Mental health; development, heredity, environ-
ment; the school, personal activity, problems of education. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 240
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: In this course the student will study the processes of communication and socialization in social interaction and in the development of the individual. The ineraction of the individual with social groups will be considered with reference to concepts such as norms, social roles, leadership-followership, attitudes, opinion and prejudices.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 310
courses.title: Psychopathology
paras: Personality and adjustment will be considered with special reference to factors related to abnormal behavior. The neuroses and psychoses, both psychogenic and organic, will be studied in some detail with regard to typical symptoms in various diagnostic categories, probable dynamics, typical therapy and prognosis. Time will also be devoted to an examination of current research on behaviour disorders. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 320
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
paras: The characteristics of sensation and perception will be studied in relation to the physics of the stimuli and physiology of the sensory apparatus. Various characteristics of perception will be studied including perceptual organization, factors of attention, illusions.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 340
courses.title: Applied Psychology
paras: This course will survey the fields of Applied Psychology and consider the application of behavioural studies to areas such as industry, education business and medicine.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 350
courses.title: Personality Theory
paras: An examination and evaluation of some of the outstanding theories of personality. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 410
courses.title: The History ot Psychology
paras: Psychological thought from the classical Greek period to the modern period with emphasis on the development of scientific psychology. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 420
courses.title: Differential Psychology
paras: The basic problems in measuring individual differences in intelligence, personality and other characteristics, will be studied. Tests will be critically examined and the application of tests to counselling, selection and guidance will be considered.
2 lectures, 1 hour laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 430
courses.title: Problems in Contemporary Psychology
paras: Conducted, for the most part, as a seminar class, the purpose of this course will be to examine the latest developments in psychology, chiefly through journal publications, so as to evaluate contemporary trends in research and theory.
2 lectures.

courses.title: Research
paras: Each student will work under the direction of a member of the department on a specific topic for scientific investigation. The results of this investigation will be presented in the form of a thesis which will be critically examined by members of the department and, also, where pertinent, by members of other departments.
